issues.description: Method getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor(): the UML in problem_statement.md declares getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor(): int (line 72), while the template repository includes a TODO comment explicitly advising a double return type (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 17) and the solution implementation declares public double getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor() (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 85). This mismatch between the UML and the suggested/implemented return type (int vs double) can confuse students about whether to implement integer division (truncating) or floating-point division (precise).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix: update the UML in problem_statement.md to declare getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor(): double and mention in the task text that a double should be returned for a precise (non-truncating) students-per-tutor calculation. Alternatively, if integer division is intended pedagogically, change the template comment and the solution method signature to return int and document the truncation behavior. Ensure tests and example outputs match the chosen type.
